headline: Genomic and transcriptomic foundation models are benchmarked against simple baselines
label: Foundation Models For Transcriptomic Prediction
summary: Recent preprints test whether learned sequence and expression representations add predictive value beyond simple baselines.
synthesis: The dominant thread is whether learned representations of genomic sequence and transcriptomes add predictive content beyond simple baselines. Evaluation-focused items include a zero-shot benchmark in which single-cell foundation model embeddings (scGPT, SCimilarity, UCE, Transcriptformer) do not consistently beat baselines, SAFFRON, which finds only Novae beats baselines on global spatial structure, and a frozen-probe analysis of five genomic language models that examines representation accessibility. Latent-space prediction recurs, most explicitly in CellWorld, which predicts latent representations of masked cells rather than reconstructing gene expression. Other work favors compact or interpretable models, including the 640-parameter SLIM and the component-wise COMPASS, while TranScouter uses LLM text inputs for cross-condition prediction. The newer emphasis is latent prediction objectives paired with explicit baseline comparison, though not every item in this set shares it.
